explanation: The default prompt names the Python target and asks for crash fixes. The same task appears in the lab before the user runs it.
workspaceState(true) restores the disposable buggy copy and runs baseline checks. The host emits this actual source and its check results before invoking the SDK.
One query receives the repair task and edit options. Read, Edit, Glob and acceptEdits are configured in lessonOptions rather than a manual tool loop.
start: const conversation = query({ prompt, options: lessonOptions(abortController) });

explanation: These option properties supply the task environment and tool definitions to the SDK. Claude API transport is performed internally by the SDK.
Actual assistant tool_use blocks are projected into tool events. The tool name and safe filename/pattern come from the observed request, not a fixed replay.
The path guard permits Read and Edit only on the disposable target. The SDK executes the built-in Read operation; this excerpt shows the application guard around it.
The SDK sends tool observations to Claude internally. The host continues consuming the same conversation and only emits its chosen projection; it has no custom tool-result sender.
An Edit request is observed through this tool_use branch just like a Read request. The actual tool name determines what happened; the app does not invent an Edit response.
The pre-tool hook accepts calls that pass toolPathAllowed and denies other targets. The SDK applies permitted edits to the working copy; the immutable fixture is not edited.
The host drains the same SDK iterator while the model can repeat inspections and edits. The final-result flag and completion check distinguish a finished run from missing evidence.
The result projection checks both subtype and is_error, preserves error variants, and exposes the actual session, estimated cost and turn count.
After closing the SDK query, the host reads the resulting file and runs independent checks through workspaceState(). The after event records whether actual source changed.
The browser renders actual source with Python syntax colours and derives Verified fix only when the source changed and all independent checks passed.
